title: OracleGroundedRecord
description: Shared envelope for oracle-grounded neuromorphic dataset records. Introduced by issue #78 for the fault-recovery, energy-preference and MoE-router distillation families; the field layout follows the shared contract sketched in parent epic #76 so the remaining families can adopt it. Enforced in code by pipelines/oracle_grounded/distill_contract.py:check_envelope — this file documents the shape, the module is the executable authority. Three invariants: a generator proposes and never certifies (generator.authority is pinned to propose_only, and oracle-measured key names may not appear anywhere inside generator/scenario/intervention/candidate_prediction); every measurement declares a quantity, a canonical unit and the meter that produced it, and energy-class quantities are only accepted from a meter that physically measures energy; producers write validation.status = 'unvalidated' and only a validator may stamp a verdict. That third invariant is not enforceable by inspecting a file — nothing stored on disk proves who wrote it — so distill_contract.curation_eligible ignores the validation block entirely and decides on the findings its caller just produced. A stamp records that a validation happened; it is not evidence that one did.

id.description: Stable record identifier, unique within a run.

family.description: Dataset family. Additional families extend this enum as they adopt the envelope.

scenario.description: Generator-owned description of the situation. May not contain oracle-measured keys.

intervention.description: Generator-owned perturbation applied to the scenario. Required by the fault-recovery family.

generator.description: Who proposed the scenario. Never an authority on the label.

authority.description: Pinned. A generator may never certify its own physical or simulator result.

model.description: Required when kind is 'llm': the model that produced the proposal.

candidatePrediction.description: The generator's guess at the answer, kept structurally distinct from the label. Every key beyond rationale/confidence/method must be named predicted_*, so a guess can never be read as a measurement.

oracle.description: What actually produced the label, and how to reproduce it.

implementation.description: module:symbol of the code that ran.

authority.description: 'reference_only' marks a stand-in whose output proves the pipeline shape but may never be curated as ground truth.

fingerprint.description: Model / checkpoint / meter identity. The MoE-router family requires model, revision_or_checkpoint, configuration_sha256 and is_llm_teacher.

measurement.description: One oracle-side reading. Energy-class quantities (energy_j, energy_per_op_j, power_w) are rejected unless meter is a real energy meter and measured is true — an operation-count or synaptic-operation model can be recorded but never substituted for a measured joule.

result.description: Oracle-owned outcome. Curation fails closed when this is missing, unmeasured, or produced by a non-authoritative oracle.

abstention_reason.description: Required when status is 'abstained'. An oracle that could not measure says so; it does not guess.

record_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical record with validation and this field removed, so stamping a verdict does not change the identity of the measured record. Required, not optional: if it may be absent, deleting it is all it takes to switch off tamper detection for the record.

validator.description: Null while unvalidated. A passed/failed verdict must name the validator that stamped it.

validated_digest.description: The record_sha256 this verdict was formed over. Catches a verdict lifted from one record onto another; it says nothing about who stamped it.
